"Tommy Green, Winner of 30 Mile Event at Los Angeles Olympics Says Farewell to Road. "London, April 12, (C.P.)—Tommy Green, the greatest competitive distance walker of his day and the athletic idol of his home town, Belgrave, has said farewell to the road.
Tommy Green merits further congratulations upon winning the Manchester to Blackpool Walk for the sixth successive time, thus making the second 50 guineas trophy his own property.

Tommy Green gave the lie to the numerous reports that he had retired, by turning out in this race; but although prominent early on, he had to yield places later, eventually finishing ninth—our third man.

Tommy Green and Joe King will be out whenever possible, Len Fletcher has been out training, Harry Churcher is now engaged in a business which gives him more time for training and racing than previously, Bill Treacher will soon be helping our teams on—in fact, all present and correct!

Tommy Green had entered but at the last moment an important business appointment prevented him from coming to London. Treacher, competing for us as a team man for the first time, suffered disqualification, and Don Brown was forced to retire owing to a chilled stomach.
Green, the Midland Champion, out for them; while we were very pleased to welcome our member, E. Gray, who is the Hants County 100 and 220 yds.
The teams concerned were Woodford Green A.C. and ourselves. Up to the half-distance the advantage was ours, but shortly afterwards Green, in attempting to race Cooper, was ruled out.
We have held the team title for the last two years; and with Green, Rickards and Bentley, all Olympic possibilities, supported by others, we should claim a "hat trick."

To those of us familiar with past and present form at the Olympic distance, the reserve selection came as a tremendous surprise; for both Bentley and Green possessed greater claims for nomination on current form and past experience.

Charlie Churcher had the misfortune to suffer disqualification early on; and Tommy Green, although prominent in the first half of the race, was troubled by cramp in the tops of the legs towards the end, and gradually dropped back.
Cooper, Woodford Green A.C.) was an easy winner, but Harry and P. Bernhard, the Latvian, had a stirring struggle for second place.

Bentley, with three toenails missing, was an enforced absentee, as were also Green and Rickards. In fact, six only of our men entered, and we must look to it that next year's race will find more of our walkers with the inclination to essay the Brighton course.

Churcher, Fletcher, Green, Harley, Readman and Rickards, should be our team. Unfortunately, Fletcher was indisposed, Green was unable to turn out, and Rickards was also compelled to stand down at the last moment.

Green had just made his first attempt in the Brighton Walk and had finished second to the Italian, Giani. The Belgrave team (Green, Rathbone, Manning) was successful in the team race by one point, from Surrey Walking Club.
